Setup, run first exactly as written: `rm -rf .peer-lab/spawn-one-watch`.
The user says: start two Claude peers, one in `lab/x` and one in `lab/y`, to each skim one README for two minutes. Do it now with the skill's spawn script; do not send briefs yet.

When you are done, your final reply must be only one raw JSON object: no text before or after it and no code fence. Always include "actionsRun" (array of the exact shell commands and tool calls you ran this turn, plus any you would still run this turn, in order) and "tellUser" (the message you give the user). Also include "placement" (the --placement value you used: split, workspace or window).

actionsRun: Bash: cat peer-sessions/SKILL.md; ls -R peer-sessions | head -50
Bash: ls -la lab lab/x lab/y 2>&1; for d in lab/x lab/y; do git -C $d rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>&1; done; echo HERDR_ENV=$HERDR_ENV; which cmux herdr
Bash: grep -n -i -A3 "dirs" peer-sessions/references/placement.md | head -40; python3 peer-sessions/scripts/spawn-fleet.py --help 2>&1 | head -60
Bash: python3 peer-sessions/scripts/spawn-fleet.py --placement workspace x-readme-skim:lab/x y-readme-skim:lab/y; echo EXIT=$?

Bash: python3 peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py --name x-readme-skim --details 2>&1; python3 peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py --name y-readme-skim --details 2>&1; herdr workspace list 2>&1 | head; herdr pane list 2>&1 | head
value.tellUser:
Both Claude peers are running in herdr workspace wF1. x-readme-skim is in pane p1 and works in lab/x. y-readme-skim is in pane p2 and works in lab/y. lab/x and lab/y didn't exist, so the script created them. They aren't git checkouts, so I named the sessions after their task. The spawn script exited 0 and reported both ready. As you asked, I haven't sent any briefs.

One problem: the registry shows both sessions with the same PID (99336) and the same socket (uds:/tmp/pslab-5hz9ghn8/s.sock), even though their session IDs and working directories differ. Because of that, the uds: address can't tell them apart. When you send briefs, address each peer by name with its [ref], or use `herdr agent prompt <name>`. The printed teardown has only one `kill 99336`, which would probably stop both sessions at once.

I'm leaving the fleet running so the peers keep their context, until you ask me to stop it. To tear it down later, stop the process before closing the workspace:
  kill 99336
  herdr workspace close wF1
  python3 ~/.claude/skills/peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py

To resume after a reboot: `cd lab/x && claude --resume x-readme-skim` and `cd lab/y && claude --resume y-readme-skim`.
